findings.issue: The onHandComplete callback and its once-per-replay-code ref guard (spec section 5, a focus point for later consumers E09/TASK-3.9) are exercised by no test. Nothing in Vitest or Playwright passes onHandComplete, so dropping the ref guard or never calling it would go unnoticed. Coverage shows useTableSession.ts at 25% lines in Vitest.
findings.evidence: grep for onHandComplete in tests/ and e2e/ finds nothing. By reading, the code is correct: StrictMode replays effects only on mount, 'done' is never the mount state, and the ref guard stops a second call when the effect re-runs because the callback's identity changed.
findings.fix: Have e2e/support/table-harness.tsx pass onHandComplete={(h) => { (window.__hands ??= []).push(h) }}. In the $10/$20 test, play to 'Hand over', wait, then assert __hands.length === 1 and that __hands[0].replayCode and userDecisions.length match. Alternatively, track it as a follow-up for TASK-3.9.

summary:
Clean build; no BLOCKER or MAJOR. session.ts is headless and pure: bots only see a PlayerView via actWith. Wrong-step calls throw the specified RangeErrors, and CompletedHand holds replay code, stakes, button, seats with starting stacks, user hole cards, every ActionRecord, board, showdownOf (engine-revealed cards only), result, and userDecisions with the PlayerView at each decision. The hook schedules exactly one setTimeout(0) per deal/bot step, clears it on cleanup (StrictMode remount and unmount safe), draws the code outside the updater, schedules nothing on 'user'/'done', ignores stale clicks via nextStep in the updater, and ref-guards onHandComplete. Mutation testing in a scratch copy outside the repo (now deleted):
- session.ts: the user-seat check, missing bot/user turn guards, decision views taken after the action, shown nulled, a wrong button, userActions off-turn and completedHand before the result were all killed by the Vitest tests. The surviving blinds/buy-in/full-view mutants are equivalent.
- UI/hook: dealing at mount was killed by the AC#1/AC#2 seated checks. Showing seated stacks only was killed by the $158/$156 and $395/$390 checks. A 300 s auto-fold timer on the user's turn was killed by the 10-minute fake-clock test, so the paused-clock helpers are not vacuous. Buttons delayed 250 ms after Dee's action were killed by the 100 ms test. Auto re-dealing after 'Hand over' was killed by the 3 s D-3 wait.
- A 400 ms artificial bot delay survives. That is consistent with A-5, whose pacing tests are deferred to TASK-3.13.
The restored copy passes table, smoke and replay-seed e2e in Chromium and WebKit (20/20). Display order Ava..Eli, You matches spec section 5 and SPEC-11/12, not a defect. Minor: onHandComplete is untested; unreachable fallbacks in completedHand.
